title: Senior Match-3 Designer, New Game
description:
We’re looking for a talented and highly experienced Senior Match-3 Designer (internally Game Designer) to join our lovely and ambitious game team and help craft fun, rewarding and memorable puzzle experiences for our cozy mobile game.

You’ll own the overall match-3 gameplay experience, helping to define how the puzzle game feels to play while delivering best-in-class levels that strike the right balance of challenge, progression and delight. From core gameplay tuning and mechanic development through to polished, data-informed level iterations, you’ll take ownership of the player experience and continually raise the quality bar.

You’ll work closely with game designers, artists, developers and analysts to ensure the match-3 is satisfying, intuitive and rewarding, evolving its mechanics, pacing and feel so that the game’s creative vision and long-term engagement goals come through. You’ll use player feedback, analytics and playtesting to refine gameplay, experiment with new ideas and shape the ongoing evolution of the game’s core puzzle experience.

As a senior member of the team, you’ll also help shape our level production strategy, driving quality with both internal development and external partners while contributing to the long-term direction of the game.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Design, build and balance exceptional match-3 levels that deliver engaging gameplay across a wide range of player skill levels.

•
Collaborate with developers to tune game feel and match 3 gameplay to be best-in-class

•
Own the design of blockers, boosters and rewards and shape satisfying level progression

•
Use analytics, player feedback and playtesting to continuously refine levels and improve player experience.

•
Work alongside Engineering to improve level design tools, workflows and implementation processes.

•
Partner with Art to ensure levels are visually readable, aesthetically cohesive and support the game’s creative vision.

•
Plan and own Match 3 content production, ensuring a consistent pipeline of high-quality content that supports development milestones and LiveOps.

•
Lead external level design contractors and outsourcing partners by providing clear briefs, regular feedback and quality reviews, ensuring all delivered content meets Treefrog’s standards.

•
Mentor other designers through feedback, knowledge sharing and collaborative problem solving.

What You Have

•
Experience shipping successful free-to-play match-3 or puzzle games.

•
Experience designing LiveOps events, seasonal content or limited-time game modes.

•
Strong understanding of player progression, retention, engagement and monetisation in puzzle.

•
Experience improving level editors, pipelines or content creation workflows.

•
Experience leading small feature teams or mentoring designers.

•
Have a deep understanding of the competition and genre trends.

•
Passion for cosy games and creating emotionally engaging player experiences.

•
A self-starter approach to use AI: you've found ways to use it in your day-to-day work, you experiment, figure things out and bring the same energy to every new challenge.

What We're Looking for

•
A strong sense of ownership, with the ability to drive work forward autonomously.

•
A consistent track record of delivering high-quality work that meets design requirements and project goals.

•
A proactive mindset, with the ability to identify opportunities and solve problems.

•
Sound judgement in balancing creative excellence with production efficiency.

•
The ability to lead external partners with clarity, empathy and high standards.

•
A collaborative approach to sharing knowledge, mentoring designers and raising the team’s quality bar.

•
Clear communication skills and the confidence to constructively challenge decisions.

•
A player-first mindset, balanced with an understanding of creative, technical and commercial goals.

•
A commitment to fostering a collaborative, inclusive and positive team culture.

Where You'll Be

This role is based in our London office. The team values in-person collaboration and typically works from the office three days a week: Mondays, Tuesdays and Fridays.

title: Art Director, Clash of Clans
description:
Clash of Clans is one of the most recognisable games ever made. We want to keep it that way, and then some.

Clash is growing beyond the game, showing up in trailers, campaigns, toys, and collaborations. The visual identity has to stretch to cover all of it, stay true to what players love, and still feel fresh. We're also modernising how we make things: pipelines are evolving, our content production is scaling, and we're working more closely with external partners than ever before.

We need someone who can own this at a strategic level. Someone who sets the vision, builds the conditions for great work, and steers the IP with confidence across every surface it touches.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Define and evolve the visual direction of Clash across the game, cosmetics, and wherever else the IP lives. True to its DNA, but never frozen in time.

•
Set the standard for style and brand fit across in-game art, marketing, trailers, toy lines, campaigns, and entertainment partners, and empower the team to uphold it.

•
Partner with game design, product, and marketing leadership to ensure art strategy supports gameplay clarity, player understanding, and long-term brand health.

•
Mentor and support Clash artists, help them do the best work of their careers while staying aligned on the IP.

•
Shape the roadmap for modernising Clash pipelines (2D to 3D, audio, tooling, and emerging technologies), championing approaches that give artists more time for the work only they can do.

•
Represent art at a senior level across the business: outsourcing partners, Entertainment and Partnerships, marketing, and franchise collaborators.

What You Have

A strong track record leading art direction on stylised games. Mobile and live-service experience is a big plus.

•
Deep IP and brand instincts, the ability to define what's on-brand vs off and build the frameworks that help a whole team make that call consistently.

•
Leadership experience on a highly collaborative senior art teams: setting vision, developing artists, and making the culture as strong as the output.

•
Strategic experience managing outsourcing pipelines and external partners at scale, balancing quality ambitions with the realities of live-game timelines and budgets.

•
Comfort operating in a low-process, high-trust environment where you own the outcomes, not just the opinions.

•
A self-starter approach to use AI. You've found ways to use it in your day-to-day work, you experiment, figure things out and bring the same energy to every new challenge.

Familiarity with Clash (as a player or from prior work) and a feel for how it's evolved.

title: Head of Editor & Tools
description:
We are looking for an exceptional leader to build and lead one of the most critical new teams in Titan: Studio Tools.

Titan is Supercell's proprietary game engine, the in-house technology that powers every game we make, reaching 300 million players a month. Titan is also the name of the roughly 70-person organization behind it.

Studio Tools brings together Titan's Editor and Art Pipelines teams under a single charter: owning everything a game team touches when making games with Titan on the client and tooling side. That means the editor, all central tooling, and the full art pipelines.

This is a visionary role. We want to build tooling that Supercell's game teams, live and new, genuinely want to use because it gives them a real edge, not tooling they tolerate, but tooling they want to depend on. We need someone entrepreneurial enough to define what world-class looks like, and capable of leading the effort to build it.

This article explains why you've probably never heard of Titan. If you want a more technical read, this one covers how Titan made Brawl Stars toilet break friendly.

Note: Internally your title will be Studio Tools Lead

What You'll Be Doing

•
Own the vision and strategy for Studio Tools team: define what Supercell's editor and tooling suite should become, and build the clarity needed to get there.

•
Define the golden path: what the ideal, yet pragmatic editor experience looks like for a Supercell game team, from day one of a new game to live games that have been running for 10+ years.

•
Set the direction for a full-featured, professional-grade editor that any new game at Supercell would choose to build on.

•
Own the Studio Tools scope end-to-end: how content is created in our games, including the editor, art pipelines, DCC tooling, and everything game teams use to interact with Titan.

•
Shape this new team from the ground up: its structure, culture, and how the combined editor and art pipelines capabilities work together.

•
Balance two demands at once with a converging toolset: actively support live game teams so they can reach their ambitions, while giving new games solutions they want from day one.

•
Lead a multi-disciplinary team of engineers, UX designers, and tech artists, setting high standards across all three disciplines and growing strong talent.

•
Contribute to Titan's leadership as a whole, not just your own team's scope.

•
Be the domain owner game teams turn to for editor, tooling, and art pipeline specifics. Understand their needs deeply and let those needs drive delivery.

•
Own the Studio Tools roadmap and its delivery across editor and art pipelines. Partner with the Product Lead, who sets Titan-level priorities and sparring on your roadmap, while you own scope, sequencing, and execution within the domain. Communicate progress clearly to game teams and Titan leadership.

What You Have

•
A track record of building and leading high-performing teams in tools, editor, or developer platform domains.

•
A deep understanding of game development workflows: you know what it takes to build tooling that artists, designers, and engineers actually want to use.

•
Visionary thinking combined with the ability to execute: you set compelling direction and build what's needed to deliver against it.

•
A good track record of people leadership across relevant disciplines.

•
An entrepreneurial mindset: you're comfortable building from scratch and taking on significant challenges with high ownership.

•
Enough technical depth to earn engineer credibility and make good judgment calls on complex trade-offs.

•
Experience building game tooling.

•
AI capability: you apply AI to change how tooling is built and experienced.

What Success In This Role Means

•
Studio Tools is a high-performing team with a clear identity and a shared sense of mission.

•
Titan has a clear editor vision and a credible plan to get there.

•
Live games are well served, and new games see Titan's tooling as a genuine competitive advantage they actively choose to build on.

Where You'll Be

The role requires close collaboration with the other central teams and game teams using the tools, so ideally, you'd be based in Helsinki.

title: Marketing Data Science Lead
description:
We’re hiring a Lead to take our Marketing Data Science team forward. About half the role is project ownership and stakeholder leadership: turning questions and needs from game teams and marketing into well-scoped Data Science work, and shipping outcomes that change decisions. The other half is craft (senior data science expertise, mobile marketing measurement and AI fluency) while being the people lead for the team.

On top of that, we expect this Lead to shape where Marketing Data Science goes next. AI is changing what’s possible in measurement, automation, and decision support faster than our roadmap. We want someone with a point of view on that, who pushes us to act on it.

You’ll report to the Head of Marketing Data and Analytics and lead a team of data scientists and analysts across a variety of data science domains and marketing functions.

The Marketing Data Science team sits behind some of Supercell’s most consequential investment decisions. We measure, model, and forecast across the full mix of marketing investments and activities: performance/UA, brand, game teams marketing and live-ops, product marketing and lifecycle, influencer and partnerships, community and social.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Make game teams better at marketing decisions. Be close to game-team marketing analysts, live-ops/monetisation leads and marketers. Translate their questions into the right modeling and measurement work.

•
Connect data science across the full marketing mix. Performance/UA, brand, product marketing and lifecycle, influencer and community, events. Each has different measurement realities. Connect them into a coherent picture.

•
Own the predictive modeling and measurement portfolio. pLTV, attribution, incrementality, brand/lifecycle, signal and audience modeling - end to end, from methodology to production to adoption.

•
Set the technical bar. Strong, opinionated view of what good looks like in applied ML, causal inference, and mobile games business data science. Hands-on when the problem needs it. Decide what ships and what doesn’t.

•
Bring AI into how the team works. Use AI tools where they actually move the work - creative media analysis, model diagnostics, automation and decisions processes.

•
Shape where the function is going. You’re not just executing a roadmap - you have a view on what Marketing Data Science should be in 6-36 months, and you push us to get there.

•
Lead and grow the team. Support, mentor, coach on stakeholder communication, set standards, hire. Make the team better than it is today.

What it might look like in practice

Representative examples of what you might tackle in your first 6-12 months.

"Are our attribution and pLTV models shaping investments?"

•
Work with Games and marketing on how they actually use attribution and profitability evaluation - in what decisions, with what trust.

•
Close the gap between model and decision quality: what measurement is for, where it stops, what we use at the edges.

"Are game teams getting what they need from us?"

•
Map what game teams actually use and where they want more, reset the cadence and format of how we deliver insight and shape ways we support marketing decisions in games.

•
Pick one game and run a quarter as a deeper partnership. Prove what “good” looks like, then scale.

"How do we measure what attribution can’t see?", "How does brand, content, and community feed performance and back?"

•
Based on a portfolio of approaches )geo experiments, holdouts, synthetic controls, MMM, lift studies and more) build algorithms for decisions on how we invest in which channels.

•
Deliver answers on how brand, influencer, and community marketing initiatives move downstream player value and translate it into a clear narrative for marketing leadership and games.

"Where does AI actually move our work?"

•
Identify 2-3 places where AI materially changes what we can do - e.g. creative analysis at scale, model-drift diagnostics, decision-support for UA and game teams.

•
Pick one. Ship it. Measure whether it actually changes work.

•
Decide what team owns internally vs. lean on the wider Data and Insights organization.

"What does “good” look like for a new game on day one?"

•
Define measurement and forecasting models before soft-launch - across the mix, not just UA.

•
Productize the approach so it doesn’t get reinvented per game.

And many other things. We expect you to take ownership, work independently, and drive the topics you believe matter.

To excel here, you

•
Own projects and stakeholders, not just models. You take a business problem and solve it - from game team conversation to shipped outcome.

•
Have deep marketing measurement craft in mobile (or close to it). Built or owned measurement work in mobile gaming, apps or other digital business verticals. Comfortable across the mix - not only performance. Understand F2P games well enough to design best-in-class measurement around them.

•
Are a senior data scientist in practice, not just title. Strong applied stats, causal inference, classical ML, coding. Hands-on with infrastructure and models in production - CI/CD, monitoring, feature stores, large-scale data warehouses, realtime inference.

•
Use AI in your own work. You’ve actually integrated AI tooling into how you do data science. You have a view on where it changes the craft and where it’s noise.

•
Communicate clearly across audiences. Able to explain a model to a game lead in three minutes. Or a methodology to a senior DS in thirty. No 100-page decks. Comfortable saying "I don’t know" and "we shouldn’t do that because".

•
Lead and grow people. Mentored or managed data analysts/data scientists. Have views on standards, best practices, when to step in, when to step back.

•
Care about games and the players. You bring a player-centric lens even when the work is deep in LLM models business applications.

•
Operate well in autonomy and ambiguity. Don’t need a pre-set structure to be productive. Comfortable being wrong, learning fast, changing direction and impact over credit.

Would Be Nice if You Also Have

•
7+ years applied Data Science / analytics with significant time in mobile gaming, apps, e-commerce or ad-tech

•
Track record of leading or significantly contributing to a data function, including hiring

•
Measurement experience across multiple types of marketing - not only performance/UA

•
Hands-on with PySpark and modern MLOps

•
Marketing measurement under modern privacy constraints (SKAN/ATT, deterministic-vs-probabilistic)

•
MMM, brand lift, and quasi-experiments design at scale

•
Concrete examples of integrating AI/LLM tooling into Data Science workflows

About the team

You’ll lead the Marketing Data Science team within Marketing Data and Analytics, as a part of the Data and Insights organisation. The wider group also includes a Marketing Data team (automation, attribution and measurement infrastructure). Your team supports all our games - Brawl Stars, Clash of Clans, Clash Royale, Hay Day, new games - and all marketing functions across the organization.

You're based in Helsinki or London. You should expect to spend significant time in Helsinki HQ with key stakeholders.

title: Default Job Posting (external)
description:
Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines.

The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist.

We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them.

In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines.

•
Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice.

•
